A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inf-SSM work. Their main texts, appendices A–J, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support a reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments, block-count ablations, CKD analyses, and Monte Carlo simulations, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds CLFD and UCL comparisons, Vim-tiny experiments, averaging-axis analysis, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix D.5 corrects the computation for nearly identical states from cos(theta)=0 to cos(theta)=1. The core observability regularizer, channel averaging, and Gram-matrix computation remain unchanged. Inf-SSM+ is retained in Appendix H.4 rather than removed. The PDFs do not establish whether the computational correction changed the implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256, and CUB-200-2011, with class-incremental learning under exemplar-free and replay settings. Additional integrations use already represented datasets and tasks; Vim-tiny changes model configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CLFD to the integration comparisons in Table 1 and UCL to the EFCIL comparisons in Table 11, substantially extending comparison across method families. ER, LUCIR, X-DER, EWC, SI, MAS, and the LwF variants remain. L2P-R is not new: it already appears in v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation with 7M-parameter Vim-tiny alongside 26M-parameter Vim-small, plus averaging-axis and batch/task latency protocols. For existing ImageNet-R LUCIR integrations, Appendix J changes the reported Inf-SSM coefficient from 10 to 500 for five tasks and from 1500 to 1000 for ten tasks. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds evidence about information retained by different averaging axes (Table 5), practical CL latency (Table 3), and sensitivity to model size (Appendix H.5). It removes v1's CKD-over-tasks analysis and Figure 3, while retaining layerwise CKD, block-count ablations, and distance-computation simulations. The Inf-SSM+ comparison is retained and regrouped.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 0, 10, and 100 and report classification results with standard deviations. The 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo studies and their correlation, p-value, and variability reporting are retained. Additional tables follow existing reporting practices; no new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds integration results on CIFAR-100 and Caltech-256, CLFD/UCL results, Vim-tiny scores, variance measurements, and CL latency measurements. Five-task ImageNet-R LUCIR baseline/augmented AA changes from 48.67/49.73 to 31.18/35.35, alongside revised reported regularization settings. Most existing Inf-SSM and Inf-SSM+ scores are retained. The new 8.31% AA and 9.36% FM integration averages agree with the expanded Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix I replaces proofs restricted to equal principal angles with general multivariate expansions establishing local equivalence of three Grassmannian distances. Appendix C.2 corrects equality of observability matrices to equality of their spanned subspaces. Appendix D.5 also corrects the normalization denominator and the cosine value for matching states.

C1.justification: The introduction's quantitative empirical contribution shifts from standalone superiority on ten-task ImageNet-R to average integration gains across three datasets and both task splits. The central claims of geometry-aware exemplar-free regularization, quadratic Sylvester computation, and compatibility with existing CL methods remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about averaging losing fine-grained variation and the computational cost of non-diagonal A. It removes v1's explicit warning that Inf-SSM+ violates orbit invariance and drops the CKD-based discussion of data-dependent need to regularize B. Section 5.1 newly interprets results as supporting sufficiency of regularizing (A,C), although the cited theorem establishes invariance.

D1.justification: Appendix J substantially expands baseline-instantiation explanations and hyperparameters for CLFD and integrations on CIFAR-100 and Caltech-256. Algorithm 1 clarifies frozen previous-model parameters and updates. Conversely, v2 removes CUB-200 hyperparameter columns, L2P pool-size/prompt-length/top-k values, and the reservoir-sampling description. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 expands coverage of CL families and SSM applications, adding citations including UCL and CLFD. Appendix J.1 develops a substantial baseline-selection and exclusion rationale, positioning other Mamba CL approaches as scenario-specific future integration targets rather than direct comparators. Much of the earlier Mamba discussion is retained in Appendix F.2.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, SSM preliminaries, method motivation, related work, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Integration results lead the revised evaluation; Inf-SSM+ moves to the appendix, limitations and conclusions are combined, and Appendix J gains structured subsections. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned into a multi-panel summary, Figure 2 moves from the appendix to the main text, and a new orbit illustration becomes Figure 3. The taskwise CKD figure is removed. Results tables are expanded, merged, relocated, and reformatted, including moving v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 6 and separating Inf-SSM+ results into Table 9.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the integration claim by extending its evidence beyond ImageNet-R to all three main datasets and additional methods. It also repairs the restricted proofs in Appendix I, corrects the invariance statement, and replaces overstated integration averages with table-supported summaries. Lost tuning details and an overstrong interpretation of (A,C) sufficiency remain drawbacks, but the stronger validation and mathematical corrections provide a substantial overall quality improvement.
